tasks.title: Scaffold backend API project with DB connection and health endpoint
acceptance: GET /health responds 200 with a minimal success body when the service is running.
The backend project boots and connects to a configured PostgreSQL database using environment variables.

tasks.title: Create Ticket and TicketEvent schema migrations (PostgreSQL)
acceptance: A migration creates a Ticket table (number, note, status, timestamps, version) and an append-only TicketEvent table.
Running the migration command against a fresh PostgreSQL database succeeds without errors.
Data persists in PostgreSQL (not in-memory) so a ticket created survives an API process restart.

tasks.title: Seed test/demo users with roles and demo data
acceptance: Running the seed command creates at least one operator user and one supervisor user with distinct roles in the database.
Seeded credentials are only intended for test/demo environments and are not real secrets committed as production values.
Running the seed command creates demonstration tickets for manual testing.

tasks.title: Implement server-session authentication with operator/supervisor roles
acceptance: Login with valid operator credentials succeeds and establishes a server session (httpOnly cookie).
Login with incorrect credentials returns a generic error that does not reveal whether the username or password was wrong.
A request to any tickets API endpoint without a valid session/token is rejected with 401 and no ticket data is returned.

tasks.title: Implement ticket creation endpoint with unique number and note validation
acceptance: POST to create a ticket without a note succeeds, returns a unique ticket number, and sets status PREPARING.
POST with a note up to 200 characters is accepted and the note is stored as provided.
Two consecutively created tickets receive distinct ticket numbers.
A POST with a note exceeding 200 characters or with invalid/missing fields is rejected by the server regardless of any client-side validation.

tasks.title: Implement ticket state transition endpoint with strict state machine and concurrency safety
acceptance: A request transitioning a ticket from PREPARING to READY succeeds and updates the stored status.
A request transitioning a ticket from READY to PICKED_UP succeeds and updates the stored status.
A request attempting to transition directly from PREPARING to PICKED_UP is rejected.
A request attempting to move a ticket backward (e.g. READY to PREPARING) is rejected.
Two concurrent transition requests on the same ticket result in a consistent final state corresponding to a single valid transition, using an atomic/optimistic-locking update.

tasks.title: Implement supervisor-only ticket cancellation endpoint preserving history
acceptance: An authenticated supervisor can cancel a ticket in PREPARING or READY status.
An attempt to cancel a ticket already in PICKED_UP status is rejected.
A cancellation request made by an authenticated operator (non-supervisor) is denied by the API with 403, independent of any UI restriction.
Cancellation records a new TicketEvent without deleting or overwriting prior history records.

tasks.title: Implement ticket list endpoint with status filter, pagination, and deterministic order
acceptance: Filtering the list by a given status returns only tickets matching that status.
Each page of results contains at most 20 tickets.
Repeated requests for the same query (filter/page) return tickets in the same order (ordered by creation date ascending, ticket number as tiebreaker).

tasks.title: Enforce server-side input validation across all ticket endpoints
acceptance: Requests with missing required fields or malformed payloads to any ticket endpoint are rejected by the server with a validation error, regardless of client-side checks.
Invalid query parameters on the list endpoint (e.g. unknown status value, out-of-range page) are rejected or safely defaulted on the server.

tasks.title: Build login UI consuming the authentication API
acceptance: Submitting valid operator credentials logs the user in and navigates to the ticket list.
Submitting incorrect credentials displays a generic error message without indicating which field was wrong.
Unauthenticated users attempting to access the ticket list view are redirected to login or blocked from seeing ticket data.

tasks.title: Build ticket list view with filter, pagination, loading/empty/error/retry states
acceptance: Selecting a status filter updates the displayed tickets to only that status.
The list paginates in pages of 20 and shows the same order on repeated loads of the same query.
A loading indicator is shown while data is being fetched.
An empty state is shown when no tickets match the current filter.
On request failure, an error state with a visible, functional retry action is shown.

tasks.title: Build ticket creation UI with optional note field
acceptance: Creating a ticket without a note succeeds and the new ticket appears with status PREPARING and a unique number.
Creating a ticket with a note up to 200 characters succeeds and the note is visible for that ticket.
Attempting to submit a note longer than 200 characters shows a client-side warning and the server rejection message if submitted.

tasks.title: Build UI controls for advancing ticket status
acceptance: An action is available to move a PREPARING ticket to READY and a READY ticket to PICKED_UP.
No UI control allows skipping directly from PREPARING to PICKED_UP or moving backward.

tasks.title: Build supervisor-only cancellation UI control
acceptance: The cancel action is visible only to users logged in as supervisor.
Cancelling a PREPARING or READY ticket as supervisor updates its displayed status and the action is unavailable for PICKED_UP tickets.

tasks.title: Render ticket notes as literal text to prevent XSS
acceptance: A ticket note containing HTML tags or script content is displayed as literal text in the UI and is never executed as HTML/script.

tasks.title: Ensure full keyboard operability and responsive layout without unjustified horizontal scroll
acceptance: All interactive controls (create, filter, change status, cancel) can be reached and activated using only the keyboard.
At a 390px viewport width, no unjustified horizontal scroll appears.
At a 1440px viewport width, no unjustified horizontal scroll appears.
Each ticket status is identifiable via text or icon in addition to color.

tasks.title: Write README with setup, env vars, migration/seed, test commands, and health endpoint docs
acceptance: README includes reproducible installation steps.
README references an example environment variables file/section containing no real secrets.
README documents the commands to run migrations and seed demo data.
README documents the commands to run unit, integration, and E2E tests.
README documents the health endpoint and its expected successful response.
